D1 Capital Partners.description: New York-based crossover investment firm founded in 2018 by Daniel Sundheim, investing across public and private markets with a focus on technology, healthcare and consumer companies.

EVP Opportunities Fund.description: Evergreen growth-stage fund launched in 2024 by Sydney-based Equity Venture Partners (EVP), backing Australian and New Zealand software and technology companies.

Fidelity Investments.description: Boston-based financial services group founded in 1946 and one of the world's largest asset managers; participates in late-stage private rounds, including Wise's secondary, alongside its public-markets business.

Fractal.description: Fractal Software is a US venture studio that funds and co-founds vertical SaaS companies with CEO/CTO pairs, providing initial capital and an operating playbook.

IA Ventures.description: New York seed-stage venture capital firm backing companies built on data and machine learning, investing from pre-seed through Series A; an investor in Wise's seed round.

InterValley Ventures.description: Melbourne-based early-stage venture capital firm (InterValley Ventures Pty Ltd) investing through its AI^Human fund in breakthrough technologies across healthcare, life sciences, agtech, fintech and edutech; an investor in StrongRoom AI.

Kalytix Ventures.description: London-based family-capital venture firm founded in 2018 by Peter Bruce-Clark to invest family capital directly into early-stage technology companies across health, infrastructure and industrial systems; an investor in StrongRoom AI.

LocalGlobe.description: London pre-seed and seed fund within Phoenix Court, backing founders across Europe at the earliest stages; sister fund to growth-stage Latitude and an investor in Wise's secondary round.

Lone Pine Capital.description: Greenwich, Connecticut investment firm founded in 1997 by Stephen Mandel Jr., investing globally across public equities and, through its private funds, growth-stage companies including Airwallex and Wise.

Mitsui & Co..description: Japanese general trading and investment company (sogo shosha) headquartered in Tokyo, investing across energy, resources, infrastructure, chemicals and innovation businesses in some 60 countries; an investor in Wise's Series E.

Old Mutual Global Investors.description: Former asset management arm of Old Mutual and an investor in Wise's Series E; renamed Merian Global Investors in its 2018 management buyout and acquired by Jupiter Fund Management in 2020, under which its funds now sit.

Sapphire Ventures.description: Global venture capital firm backing expansion-stage enterprise software and AI companies, with around US$10 billion under management across Menlo Park, San Francisco, Austin and London; an investor in Culture Amp and Wise.

Tyson & Blake.description: London-based investment and advisory firm investing internationally in growth-stage companies; an investor in Australian health-technology company StrongRoom AI's Series A.

Valar Ventures.description: New York venture capital firm founded in 2010 by Andrew McCormack, James Fitzgerald and Peter Thiel, investing in high-growth technology — historically fintech — companies outside Silicon Valley; led Wise's Series A.

Vulcan Capital.description: Investment arm formed in 2003 by Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen to manage his technology and growth investments, including Wise's secondary round; its team and strategy spun out as the independent firm Cercano Management in 2021.

World Innovation Lab.description: World Innovation Lab (WiL) is a US–Japan growth-stage venture capital firm partnering with corporate investors to back startups expanding between the US and Asia; an investor in Wise's Series E.
